jaxR

jaxR is an R mirror of JAX: composable transformations of array programs (grad, vmap, jit, jvp, vjp, linearize, jacfwd, jacrev, hessian, checkpoint), a NumPy compatible array API, lax primitives with structured control flow, counter based random numbers whose bits agree with JAX exactly, and SciPy style special functions, linear algebra and FFTs.

Like JAX, jaxR traces R functions to an intermediate representation (jaxpr), lowers it to StableHLO and compiles it with XLA. The XLA runtime is a PJRT plugin loaded at run time, in the way rstan embeds Stan or torch uses libtorch; nothing is translated from Python at run time and no Python installation is needed.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("adamrsophie/jaxR")
jaxR::install_pjrt()   # downloads the XLA CPU runtime (once)

Prebuilt runtimes are available for Linux and macOS, on x86-64 and arm64. Set JAXR_PJRT_PLUGIN to use another PJRT plugin (for example a CUDA build). There is no prebuilt runtime for Windows: the package installs there, and it needs JAXR_PJRT_PLUGIN to name a PJRT plugin built for Windows.

A quick tour 

library(jaxR)

f <- function(x) sum(sin(x) * x)
x <- as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))

grad(f)(x)                      # reverse mode
jit(grad(f))(x)                 # compiled by XLA
vmap(grad(f))(jnp_stack(list(x, 2 * x)))
hessian(f)(x)

# Structured control flow is differentiable and compiles
g <- function(v) lax_scan(function(c, xi) list(c * 0.5 + xi, c * xi), 0, v)[[2]]
grad(function(v) sum(g(v)))(x)

# Random numbers: same keys, same bits as JAX
key <- random_key(0L)
k <- random_split(key)
random_normal(k[1], c(3L, 2L))

Conventions

  • Names follow JAX modules: jax.numpy.sum is jnp_sum, jax.lax.scan is lax_scan, jax.random.normal is random_normal, jax.scipy.special.gammaln is scipy_special_gammaln, jax.nn.relu is nn_relu. Transformations keep their JAX names (grad, vmap, jit, …). No jaxR function masks a base R function.
  • Axes, indices, argnums and in_axes are 0-based, as in JAX: x[0] is the first element and jnp_sum(x, axis = 0L) reduces the first dimension. Python style slices are written sl(start, stop, step).
  • As in JAX, arrays are 32-bit by default. Use enable_x64() (or set JAX_ENABLE_X64=1) for 64-bit floats and integers.
  • R scalars are weakly typed, so x * 2 keeps the dtype of x.
  • Arrays live on the device; as.array(x) returns R data. Use as.logical(x) in if conditions.

Symbolic computation

jaxR works with symcompR: jax_lambdify(args, expr) turns a symbolic expression into a jaxR function that can be differentiated, vectorized and compiled, and grad() / hessian() forward symbolic expressions to symcompR.

Status

jaxR follows JAX 0.12.0.1. The transformations, jax.numpy, jax.lax, jax.random, jax.nn, jax.scipy, jax.image, jax.tree_util, jax.experimental.sparse and the example libraries (stax, optimizers) are ported and tested against values produced by JAX itself. Features that need several devices (pmap across devices, sharding, distributed arrays) are not ported; named axis collectives (lax_psum, lax_all_gather, …) work under vmap(..., axis_name = ). The vignettes describe each area and list the differences from JAX.
